title: Claim records and what a coding agent says: four preregistered experiments — replication package
description: Four preregistered experiments (a pilot and three studies, 6,224 trials, Claude Haiku 5.5 as a coding agent on tasks with hidden checks) on whether a signed, hash-chained record of the agent's own claims changes what it claims and what it delivers. Publishing the record showed no detectable effect on false completion claims. Asking for a record with evidence (instruction, tool and signed record together) lowered false completion by 6.6 points and raised false non-completion by 27.9 points; a 'complete' claim was not more often true and the share of finished work was about the same. Pressure framing and independent acceptance tests showed no gain on the confirmatory tests. The completion labeller was not validated by a person. Ships the preregistrations, the per-trial scores, the frozen analysis outputs, the labeller audit, tests that lock the published numbers and a SHA-256 provenance seal.
